title: "F-gsig — Group signature"
status: "Emerging"
layer: 7
definition: "Not yet written"
---

*F-gsig* (Group signature) is part of *Privacy and Anonymity* in the UC functionality encyclopedia. Status: an emerging formulation, still an active area of research.

Every English-language, peer-reviewed treatment of group signatures found (Bellare–Micciancio–Warinschi, Bellare–Shi–Zhang, Kiayias–Yung, Camenisch–Groth, Bootle et al., and Wikström's own thesis below) is game-based, not a UC ideal functionality. The one paper found with a boxed *F-GSIG* is an unreviewed domestic-symposium manuscript (see caveat below) — hence this page's "Emerging" status.

*References:*

- Makita, Manabe, and Okamoto. [*On Universally Composable Group Signatures*](https://security-kouza.github.io/paper/scis2005_makita.pdf). In SCIS 2005 (The 2005 Symposium on Cryptography and Information Security), 2005. Note: SCIS proceedings are explicitly circulated without peer review — this is the only paper found with a boxed UC functionality for group signatures, but it has not been independently vetted.
- Wikström. [*On the Security of Mix-Nets and Hierarchical Group Signatures*](https://kth.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:14421/FULLTEXT01.pdf). PhD thesis, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, 2005.
